t: In this town, you're not allowed to die. Well… sort of.
Longyearbyen, on the Arctic islands of Svalbard. About twenty-four hundred people, and more polar bears around than you'd like.
Here, the ground never thaws. It's permafrost.
So in the nineteen fifties, the tiny cemetery stopped taking new burials. Bodies here simply don't decay.
In nineteen ninety-eight, scientists even dug up victims of the nineteen eighteen flu, to look for traces of the virus.
That's why, if you get seriously ill here, you're flown to mainland Norway.
Babies aren't born here either. Moms-to-be leave weeks before their due date.
It's not actually a law. But in Longyearbyen, nobody plans to stay forever.
Would you live in a town where you can't be buried? Tell me in the comments.
